item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 080514
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Oct 7 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Simon, located
more than 100 miles southwest of coast of the Mexican state of
Guerrero.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala during the early portion of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for some gradual development of this
system thereafter, and a tropical depression could form as it moves
generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Simon are issued under WMO
header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Simon are issued under WMO
header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Papin

Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  45
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026
 
...RACHEL NOW A TROPICAL STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.8N 123.9W
ABOUT 895 MI...1445 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...985 MB...29.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 21.8 North, longitude 123.9 West. Rachel is
moving toward the west-northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). This general 
motion is expected to continue over the next 24 hours, before a 
sharp turn to the northeast, along with an increase in forward 
speed, is forecast to occur. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Continued gradual weakening is expected over the 
next few days. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 985 mb (29.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header
WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the
weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions.  Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 45
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 080841
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  45
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026

Dry air continues to eat away at Rachel's convection. Satellite 
imagery over the last couple of hours depicts noticeable degradation 
across the western semicircle, with deep convection weakening 
throughout the storm as seen through warming cloud-top temperatures. 
While TAFB's subjective Dvorak intensity estimate was unchanged at 
4.0/65 kt, objective estimates from UW-CIMSS have trended downward. 
As a result of this, combined with the weakening trend seen through 
satellite imagery, the initial intensity was set at 60 kt, and 
Rachel has been downgraded to a Tropical Storm.

The initial motion was estimated at 290/7 kt. Rachel appears to have 
gained a slight amount of speed since last advisory, its motion 
driven primarily by high pressure anchored over the southwestern US. 
However, a mid- to upper-level trough currently sweeping across the 
Pacific is forecast to pick up Rachel and turn it to the northeast 
in approximately 24 hours. This will coincide with an increase in 
forward speed. While track guidance continues to exhibit a fair 
amount of spread after this trough interaction, skilled guidance has 
become more aligned on a solution since the last advisory. The 
latest NHC track forecast nudges Rachel's trajectory more towards 
HCCA and GDMI, which results in a slight shift toward the right as 
the storm the storm approaches northern Baja California. 

As Rachel continues to move about in an environment characterized by 
cooling SSTs and dry mid-level air, its convection is expected to 
further degrade, thus inducing further weakening. Once the 
aforementioned trough shifts Rachel's path, vertical wind shear is 
also expected to increase substantially, leading to even further 
weakening as the storm approaches northern Baja California and 
southern California. Simulated satellite imagery even suggests that 
Rachel may lose its deep convection altogether by the time it hits 
land, however strong winds and heavy rain can still be expected 
wherever Rachel makes landfall, either as a tropical storm or a 
post-tropical cyclone. The latest NHC intensity forecast reflects a 
more steady weakening trend compared to the previous advisory, with 
Rachel forecast to become post-tropical between 72 and 96 hours, or 
shortly after making landfall. 

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of extreme northern Baja 
California and Southern California at or near tropical storm 
strength over the weekend, potentially bringing strong winds and 
coastal flooding to portions of those areas. Gusty winds could 
spread over interior portions of the Southwest United States into 
early next week.
 
2. Moisture associated with Rachel will spread over portions of the 
Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula 
through this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of 
rainfall and a threat of flash and urban flooding.
 
3. Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast of
Southern California and northern Baja California through the
weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions.  Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

ABOUT 190 MI...305 KM SSW OF LAZARO CARDENAS MEXICO
ABOUT 260 MI...420 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
The government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Watch from
Punta San Telmo to Manzanillo.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Manzanillo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.

Additional watches could be required for portions of the coast of 
southwestern Mexico later today. 
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was
located near latitude 15.4 North, longitude 103.1 West. Simon is
moving toward the west near 7 mph (11 km/h) and this motion is 
expected to continue through today, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest to north-northwest on Friday.  Simon should turn 
toward the north Friday night and approach the coast of 
southwestern Mexico on Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Rapid strengthening is forecast, and Simon is expected to 
become a major hurricane by late Friday or early Saturday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch area 
early Friday.
 
RAINFALL:  Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 12
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals between 15 and 25 inches possible across portions of Colima
and Michoacan through Sunday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Thu Oct 08 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 080855
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Thu Oct 08 2026
 
This evening's conventional satellite imagery and a recent ASCAT
overpass and a 0323 UTC MetOp-SG1 MI indicate that Simon is
developing a compact inner core structure.  There are also curved
bands with -73C to -82C cold cloud tops forming in the west and
northeast portions of the cyclone.  The TAFB subjective satellite
intensity estimate is T3.0/45 kt and a blend of the UW-CIMSS
objective estimates (41-47 kt) yield an initial intensity of 45 kt.
 
The shear is low, the atmosphere is moist, and the ocean is warm
with high heat content values, all contributing to a high
probability of Simon quickly intensifying during the next couple of
days.  The upper wind pattern is also quite favorable with 
impressive diffluent easterly flow ventilating the western portion 
of the cyclone.  The latest SHIPS RI Index shows a 63 percent 
chance of a 55 kt increase in 48 hrs, while the UW-CIMSS AI-RI 
indicates a similar likelihood of rapid intensification.  The 
official forecast shows Simon becoming a major hurricane in 48 hrs 
with a peak intensity of 115 kt on Saturday, and this is based on 
the HFIP-HCCA and slightly above the Google DeepMind ensemble 
guidance.
 
Simon's initial motion is estimated to be due west, or 270 degrees 
at 6 kt.  This general motion should continue through today while 
being steered by high pressure north of the cyclone over central 
Mexico.  On Friday, the system should turn west-northwestward to 
north-northwestward in response to a mid-tropospheric trough 
approaching Baja California.  Toward the end of the period, Simon is 
expected to move northward ahead of and on the southeastern side of 
the aforementioned trough and approach the southwestern coast of 
Mexico over the weekend.  The GFS and the ECMWF HiRes global models 
still show outlier tracks to the left of the NHC forecast but have 
been trending eastward, aligning more with the better-performing 
HCCA and Google DeepMind TC ensemble mean aids, which the official 
forecast leans toward.
 
Simon's 34 kt wind radii were decreased a bit based on a 0403 UTC
METOP-B ASCAT pass.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by early Friday 
and approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane 
on Saturday. Tropical storm conditions are possible within the 
tropical storm watch area early Friday. There is also risk of 
dangerous wind and storm surge impacts along portions of this coast 
over the weekend and into early next week and additional watches 
will likely be required for portions of southwestern Mexico.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico later this week and into the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend.  These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please
consult products from your local weather office.
